description: A 16th-century fort near Delhi Zoo on Mathura Road, on the site of the ancient city of Indraprastha. Humayun built its walls and gateways and Sher Shah Suri carried the work forward. It hosts a sound and light show every evening.
verifiedNote: Official source for prices and metro. Opening hours are not on the official page and come from travel sites.

name: Humayun’s Tomb
description: A magnificent garden tomb near the crossing of Mathura Road and Lodhi Road, and the first substantial example of Mughal architecture in India. It was built in 1565 by Humayun’s senior widow Bega Begum, and the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah II was captured here in 1857.
verifiedNote: Official source. Lower online prices appear on other sites.

name: Qutub Minar
partialNote: Parts of the complex are closed for repairs (ASI report, Sept 2026).
description: A 72.5 m tower of red and buff sandstone begun in 1199 as a call-to-prayer tower. It is the tallest tower in India, and each storey has a balcony with honeycomb-patterned brackets.
source: ASI and Delhi Tourism (official); travel sites
verifiedNote: Official source. Some other sites list a ₹40 counter price for Indians. Booking link: ASI official page, which has the Book Online Entry Ticket button.

name: Safdarjung Tomb

description: The last enclosed garden tomb in Delhi, in the tradition of Humayun’s Tomb but smaller, built in 1753–54 for Safdarjung, the viceroy of Awadh. Its pavilions include Jangli Mahal, Moti Mahal and Badshah Pasand, and the complex has a madarsa and an ASI library over the main gateway.

name: Jantar Mantar
partialNote: Parts are restricted while repairs are underway.
description: An observatory built in 1724 by Maharaja Jai Singh of Jaipur, with large stone instruments such as the Samrat Yantra sundial. Accurate observations can no longer be made here because of the tall buildings around.

name: Feroz Shah Kotla
description: A 14th-century Tughlaq-era fort with thick walls, bastions, a mosque, a tomb and a stepwell. An Ashokan pillar brought from Haryana stands inside.
verifiedNote: Checked 17 Nov 2026. Not confirmed by an official source.

name: Lodhi Garden tombs
description: The old Lady Willingdon Park, now Lodhi Garden, beside the India International Centre on Lodhi Road. It is dotted with tombs, mosques and bridges of the Sayyid and Lodhi periods, including the octagonal tombs of Muhammad Shah and Sikandar Lodhi and the square Shish Gumbad and Bara Gumbad.
verifiedNote: Official source says morning to evening. Some travel sites say 6 AM – 8 PM in winter.

name: Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah
description: A Sufi shrine honouring the 14th-century saint Nizamuddin Auliya and his disciple Amir Khusro. Qawwali sessions on Thursdays draw large crowds.
verifiedNote: Checked 17 Nov 2026. Not confirmed by an official source.

name: India Gate
description: A 42 m high arch near Rajpath, designed by Edwin Lutyens and dedicated in 1931. It commemorates the 70,000 Indian soldiers lost in World War I, and the Amar Jawan Jyoti flame was added after 1971. It is floodlit at night and the lawns around it are a popular picnic spot.
verifiedNote: Official source says morning to night. Other sites say open 24 hours.

name: Lotus Temple
description: A Bahá’í house of worship near Kalkaji Temple, built in the shape of a lotus and completed in 1986. It is made of white marble and set among landscaped gardens with nine pools, and people of any faith can visit to pray or meditate.

name: Akshardham Temple
description: Swaminarayan Akshardham, opened in 2005, shows 10,000 years of Indian culture through its temple, exhibitions, a musical fountain and the Garden of India. It was built in five years and is recognised by Guinness World Records as the world’s largest comprehensive Hindu temple.
verifiedNote: Official source. Some other sites say the complex stays open until 8 PM.

description: The largest mosque in India, in Old Delhi, with a courtyard for 25,000 people. It was begun in 1644 as Shah Jahan’s last grand building, with three great gates, four towers and two 40 m minarets of red sandstone and white marble.
verifiedNote: Official source. Some other sites list different foreign entry and camera fees.

name: Birla Mandir (Laxminarayan Temple)
description: Laxmi Narayan Temple, known as Birla Mandir, is one of Delhi’s major temples, built by industrialist J.K. Birla in 1939 near Gole Market. It is dedicated to Laxmi and Narayana and was inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi on the condition that people of all castes could enter.
verifiedNote: Official source. The official page does not list days closed. Best to visit during morning and evening aarti.

name: Adventure Island
description: Amusement and water park beside Metro Walk mall in Rohini, with thrill rides, family rides, water rides and games, so you can spend the whole day.
thingsToKnow: Thrill rides include Z-Force, Side Winder and Sky Riders; water rides include Aqua Bump and Splash Pool.
SkyJumper trampoline park is a separate paid attraction inside the park, according to reviewers.
Swimwear is on sale for water rides, and changing rooms have showers.
Some rides may be closed on the day, so check before you go.
Opening hours can change with the weather.
source: Delhi Tourism listing (delhitourism.travel, updated 17 Oct 2025) and District ticket page
verifiedNote: Prices differ between sources (₹500–₹600 against "from ₹699"). No official booking link found. Check before you go.

name: Fun N Food Village
description: Water and amusement park with more than 20 rides, water slides, a snow park, an 800 ft lazy river, a rain dance area and a kids' zone, with food courts inside.
thingsToKnow: Delhi Tourism lists rides such as Magic Carpet and Rock n Roll, plus a kids' pool and play zone.
Another site says ticket counters close at 4:00 PM and the park shuts at 6:00 PM.
Swimwear is needed for the water slides.
source: Delhi Tourism (delhitourism.gov.in) for hours and rides; ticket prices from Plumint (2025)
verifiedNote: Delhi Tourism gives no ticket prices. Another site lists ₹500 onwards and closing at 6 PM, so prices and hours are unverified. The Delhi Tourism page also gives a Defence Colony address that does not match Kapashera.
